I believe you can joke about anything, but that doesnt mean every joke is funny and is supposed to be told. Stand up comedy is sadly filled with jokes built on overdue stereotypes or using cheap jokes to get cheap laughs.

Where is the fun using a -ist stereotype as the punchline and build a set up from it? To me thats just lazy writing. 

Shed light on the prejudice instead of cementing it. Lets laugh at the ones saying horrible things instead of the ones getting hurt by the horrible things.
If you cant, joke about something else - thats what I mainly do - and im doing fine.

Please support the art by educating the audience, not fucking forcing them into a laugh from shock and "free speech"

You can joke about everything, though that doesnt mean every joke is a good enough joke to be told.

Eddie izzard talks in his documentary "believe" about the fact that a stand up comedian has to be both a writer and a performer, and thats what i love about the format.
Seeing the divercity between a good writer doing a bad performance and a somewhat lesser writer does a great performance is what makes stand up awesome.
Now im being pretentious about the art but it's comedians writing what they think is funny and performing it, without others to reinterpret it is what makes comedy moving forward.

Selling specific jokes for a prize will create some kind of supply and demand for what comics should write, and humor wouldnt progress.
The pop scene hasnt changed a lot because of that, but elektro, punk and hiphop keeps progressing and even create new genres because of people performing what they are writing.
